For a fixed residue $i$ list the addable and removable $i$-nodes of a partition
**by increasing content** $c-r$; larger content is read as further right or
higher. For an addable $i$-node $\gamma$ of $\lambda$ (so that
$\mu=\lambda+\gamma$) define

$$N_i^r(\lambda,\gamma):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes of }\lambda\text{ with content}>\text{content}(\gamma)\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes of }\lambda\text{ with content}>\text{content}(\gamma)\},$$

and for a removable $i$-node $\gamma$ of $\mu$ (so that
$\lambda=\mu-\gamma$) define $N_i^l(\lambda,\mu)$ by the same formula inside the
smaller diagram $\lambda=\mu-\gamma$ with $>$ replaced by $<$, always excluding
$\gamma$ itself. The node formulas are then

$$F_i|\lambda\rangle=\sum_{\gamma}q^{N_i^r(\lambda,\gamma)}|\lambda+\gamma\rangle,\qquad E_i|\mu\rangle=\sum_{\gamma}q^{-N_i^l(\mu-\gamma,\mu)}|\mu-\gamma\rangle,$$

over the addable respectively removable $i$-nodes. The **node order** is the
content order just fixed, and it is used to define the finite signature
selection: a Chevalley coefficient minimiser is not in general a Kashiwara
arrow, and even a nonzero single Chevalley term can have zero crystal arrow.

The constructed node operators on **all** partition vectors make the charge-$0$
partition Fock space $F$ into a $P$-graded integrable module for
$U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_e)$ with the fixed coproduct and the cyclic Cartan
datum: all toral commutation rules and mixed commutators
$[E_i,F_j]=\delta_{ij}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ hold, and both quantum Serre
sums vanish, including the cubic $e=2$ case with
$a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ and $[3]=q^2+1+q^{-2}$. Each color acts on finite Boolean
cubes, and $F_i,E_i$ change the $P$-weight by $\mp\alpha_i$. Ordinary standard
coefficients may have $q^{-1}$ poles; normalized Kashiwara lattice stability is
a separate statement.

Work over $\mathbb Q(q)$ with a symmetrizable Cartan datum of type $A$ as in
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], put $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and let
$B$ be a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra equipped with elements
$E_i,F_i,K_h^{\pm1}$ ($i\in I$, $h\in P^\vee$) satisfying the toral and
toral-action relations and the mixed commutators
$E_iF_j-F_jE_i=\delta_{ij}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]; let $W$ be a $B$-module with a chosen integral label grading on which $K_h$ acts by $q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}$ on $W_\mu$, and $E_i,F_i$ shift labels by $\pm\alpha_i$. Assume that $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on $W$ for every $i$ (rank-one integrability). Then the negative quantum Serre sums

$$\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r=0\qquad(i\ne j)$$

vanish as operators on $W$, and, by the Chevalley interchange
$E_i\leftrightarrow F_i$, $K_h\leftrightarrow K_{-h}$, so do the positive sums
$\sum_{r}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r$. In particular the
$e=2$ cubic sums with $a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ hold. No Serre relation is assumed.

derivations.claim: The vanishing cases. Every $E$ monomial removes four cells, so all four outputs on $\varnothing,1,2,11$ vanish. For $F$ on $\varnothing$, $F_1\varnothing=0$ and $F_0\varnothing=1$, $F_0 1=0$; these kill all four compositions. On $1,3,111$, the three compositions with a rightmost $F_0$ vanish because $F_0$ kills each input. For the remaining $F_0^3F_1$, the node formulas give $F_0^2F_1|1\rangle=0$, $F_0^2F_1|3\rangle=(q^{-2}+1)|321\rangle$, and $F_0^2F_1|111\rangle=(q^{-1}+q)|321\rangle$; in both latter cases $F_0|321\rangle=0$ since it has no addable $0$-node. Thus each of the four $F$ outputs on the stated boundary inputs is zero.

The size-$2$ cancellations. Starting from $|2\rangle$ and applying the four ordered compositions via [F1] gives the first output as $[3](q^{-2}+1)|3,2,1\rangle$, the second as $(q^{-2}+1)|3,2,1\rangle$, and the last two $0$: indeed the coefficient of $|321\rangle$ in the leading output is $q^{-4}+2q^{-2}+2+q^2=[3](q^{-2}+1)$ and the other outputs contribute the same multiple of the middle term; cancelling gives $0$. The same computation from $|1,1\rangle$ gives outputs $([3]B,B,0,0)$ with $B=(q^{-1}+q)|321\rangle$ because the coefficient is $q^{-3}+2q^{-1}+2q+q^3=[3](q^{-1}+q)$.
Noncommutation. Direct evaluation gives $F_0F_1|1\rangle=|3\rangle+q|1,1,1\rangle$ and $F_1F_0|1\rangle=0$, since $F_0|1\rangle=0$; hence the ordinary generators do not commute.

The size-$3$ cancellations. From $|2,1\rangle$ the second composition yields the common term $C$, the third yields $D$, and the fourth yields $[3](D-C)$, so the sum contributes $[3](-C+D-(D-C))=0$ coefficientwise; from $|3,2,1\rangle$, applying the $E$-compositions gives the last output $[3]Z$ with the stated $Z$, and the first two outputs vanish, while the third output is $Z$; the sum vanishes.

Conclusion. The displayed finite chains exhibit the double-edge Serre cancellation on $2,11,21$ and the $E$ cancellation on $321$, with the $[3]$ coefficients $q^2+1+q^{-2}$; the general relation including the colour swap is proved by the independent rank-one Serre lemma, so no finite diagnostic is promoted to a universal proof.

There is an explicit semi-infinite wedge bar $\psi$ with the vacuum fixed,
coefficient bar $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ and $U_q$/bar compatibility, whose restriction
to $M=V(\Lambda_0)$ is the normalized highest module bar. On **all** partitions
its integral triangular correction is

$$G(\lambda)=|\lambda\rangle+\sum_{\mu\ \text{strictly dominated by}\ \lambda}d_{\mu,\lambda}(q)|\mu\rangle, \qquad d_{\mu,\lambda}\in q\mathbb Z[q],$$

with diagonal $1$ and same $e$-core support; the family $\{G(\lambda)\}$ is an
$A$-basis of $F_A$ and an $A_0$-basis of $F_0$, with the actual infinity chart
and balanced $\mathbb Z$-intersection. Exactly the $e$-regular $G(\lambda)$ form
the lower global basis of $M$, identified by the two lower-global-basis
suppliers. The ambient basis is not automatically compatible with the other
field irreducible summands. The transpose equality
$d_{\lambda,\mu}=d_{\mu',\lambda'}$ is **false** in general; the source symmetry
concerns the bar matrix, not $D$. Ambient natural-form dual coefficients use
$(D^{-1})^{\mathsf T}$, and basic upper coefficients require the restricted Gram
inverse and need not be Laurent polynomials.

Let $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ be partitions of the same integer $n$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). We say that
$\lambda$ **dominates** $\mu$, and write $\lambda\unrhd\mu$, exactly when
$$\sum_{i=1}^{r}\lambda_i\;\ge\;\sum_{i=1}^{r}\mu_i\qquad\text{for every }r\ge1,$$
where each sequence is padded with zeros beyond its number of parts; since both
partitions have total $n$, both sides equal $n$ for all $r$ at least the number
of parts of either, so the condition is a finite family of inequalities between
integers. We write $\lambda\rhd\mu$ when $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ and
$\lambda\ne\mu$. The relation $\unrhd$ is the **dominance order** on the
partitions of $n$; we call $\lambda$ and $\mu$ **incomparable** when neither
$\lambda\unrhd\mu$ nor $\mu\unrhd\lambda$ holds.

Because it is defined by a family of non-strict inequalities between integers,
$\unrhd$ is reflexive and transitive. It is also antisymmetric: if
$\lambda\unrhd\mu$ and $\mu\unrhd\lambda$, then the prefix sums of $\lambda$ and
of $\mu$ are equal for every $r\ge1$, and subtracting consecutive prefix sums
gives $\lambda_i=\mu_i$ for every $i$ (both sequences are eventually zero).
Hence $\unrhd$ is a partial order on the set of partitions of $n$. For $n\ge1$,
the partition $(n)$ is its unique maximum and the partition $(1^n)$ its unique
minimum: for every $\mu\vdash n$ and every $r\ge1$ one has
$$\min(r,n)=\sum_{i\le r}(1^n)_i\;\le\;\sum_{i\le r}\mu_i\;\le\;n=\sum_{i\le r}(n)_i .$$

For $n=0$ the order is the trivial order on the one-element set
$\{\varnothing\}$.

A partition is **regular** if each positive part occurs with multiplicity $<e$,
and **restricted** if $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}<e$ for every $r$. Conjugation
$C:\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ is the comparison map between the regular and the
restricted models; it sends the residue $i$ to $-i$. It is **not** the
same-model sign involution.

On the regular basic crystal of
[[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]] define
$M$ by negating all colors of a lowering path from the empty partition:
$M(f_ib)=f_{-i}M(b)$ for every edge, $M(\varnothing)=\varnothing$. The
restricted sign involution is the conjugate $CMC^{-1}$.

derivations.claim: The degrees $\le3$. Solving the triangular bar equations degree by degree with the reversal bar: in degree $2$ the only correction of $2$ is $q\,11$; in degree $3$ the partition $21$ is the only shape whose residue multiset forces no correction and $3$ receives the correction $q\,111$; the remaining shapes are bar-fixed. This gives the displayed degree-$\le3$ elements, and the basic labels are the $2$-regular ones, namely $\varnothing,1,2,3,21$, with $11$ and $111$ non-regular.

The degree-four bar calculation. The finite reversal formula of [F1], at any cutoff longer than four, and straightening give $\psi|4\rangle=|4\rangle+(q-q^{-1})|31\rangle+(q^{-2}-1)|22\rangle+(q^2-1)|1111\rangle$, $\psi|31\rangle=|31\rangle+(q-q^{-1})|22\rangle+(q^2-1)|211\rangle$, $\psi|22\rangle=|22\rangle+(q-q^{-1})|211\rangle+(q^{-2}-1)|1111\rangle$, $\psi|211\rangle=|211\rangle+(q-q^{-1})|1111\rangle$ and $\psi|1111\rangle=|1111\rangle$. Substituting these five formulas, with coefficient bar, verifies the displayed columns $G(4)=|4\rangle+q|31\rangle+q|211\rangle+q^2|1111\rangle$, $G(31)=|31\rangle+q|22\rangle+q^2|211\rangle$, $G(22)=|22\rangle+q|211\rangle$, $G(211)=|211\rangle+q|1111\rangle$ and $G(1111)=|1111\rangle$: each is bar fixed with its stated leading residue and coefficients in $q\mathbb Z[q]$. Uniqueness in [F1] therefore identifies them with the lower lifts. The basic labels are the regular shapes $4,31$, and the nonzero positions visibly respect dominance.

The false transpose symmetry. Conjugation of partitions sends $211\mapsto31$ and $4\mapsto1111$, so the transpose-conjugation equality would require $d_{(211),(4)}=d_{(1111),(31)}$; but the degree-$4$ matrix gives $d_{(211),(4)}=q$ and $d_{(1111),(31)}=0$. Hence the equality fails in general; the source's symmetry statement concerns the bar transition matrix $A$, not the lower matrix $D$.

Conclusion. The displayed elements are the actual lower global basis elements in degrees $\le4$, their coefficients are integral and dominance-triangular, the basic columns are the regular labels, and the naive transpose symmetry of $D$ is refuted by the explicit pair.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Fix an integer $e\ge 2$ and put $I:=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z=\{0,1,\dots,e-1\}$
with its cyclic order; elements of $I$ are called **residues**. Let
$A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ be the integer matrix with

$$a_{ii}=2,\qquad a_{i,i-1}=a_{i,i+1}=-1\ \ (i\in I)$$

when $e\ge 3$, and with $a_{00}=a_{11}=2$ and the single double edge
$a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ when $e=2$; all indices are read modulo $e$. Thus for
$e\ge3$ all off-diagonal entries other than the neighbouring entries $-1$ are
$0$, and for $e=2$ the matrix is
$\begin{pmatrix}2&-2\\-2&2\end{pmatrix}$. Take the diagonal symmetrizer
$D=\operatorname{diag}(1,\dots,1)$ and the quantum parameter $q$ over
$\mathbb Q$, so that $q_i=q^{d_i}=q$ for every $i\in I$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]).

Choose free abelian groups

$$P=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\Lambda_i\Bigr)\oplus\mathbb Z\delta, \qquad P^{\vee}=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z h_i\Bigr)\oplus\mathbb Z d,$$

with the $\mathbb Z$-bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times
P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$ determined by

$$\langle\Lambda_j,h_i\rangle=\delta_{ij},\qquad \langle\delta,h_i\rangle=0,\qquad \langle\Lambda_j,d\rangle=0,\qquad \langle\delta,d\rangle=1 .$$

Define the **simple roots**

$$\alpha_i:=\sum_{j\in I}a_{ji}\Lambda_j+\delta_{i0}\,\delta\qquad(i\in I),$$

let $Q:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ be the **root lattice**
and $Q^+$ its nonnegative cone, and define the **central element**
$c:=\sum_{i\in I}h_i\in P^{\vee}$. The **level** of $\lambda\in P$ is
$\langle c,\lambda\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
and the **classical weight lattice** is $P_{\mathrm{cl}}:=P/\mathbb Z\delta$.

The **diagram reflection** $\tau$ is the pair of $\mathbb Z$-linear
involutions $\tau:P\to P$, $P^{\vee}\to P^{\vee}$ with
$\tau(\Lambda_i)=\Lambda_{-i}$, $\tau(\delta)=\delta$, $\tau(h_i)=h_{-i}$ and
$\tau(d)=d$ (indices negated in $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$).

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $t$ be an indeterminate over $\mathbb Q$, and let $A$ be a unital associative $\mathbb Q(t)$-algebra. For $N\ge0$ and $0\le r\le N$, set

$$B_{N,r}(t):=\frac{[N]_t!}{[r]_t![N-r]_t!},\qquad [m]_t:=1+t+\cdots+t^{m-1},\quad [m]_t!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_t,\quad [0]_t:=0,\quad [0]_t!:=1,$$

and set $B_{N,r}(t)=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>N$. If $x,y\in A$ satisfy $yx=txy$, then for every $N\ge0$,

$$ (x+y)^N=\sum_{r=0}^{N}B_{N,r}(t)x^ry^{N-r}.$$

For a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, any unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra can be viewed as a $\mathbb Q(t)$-algebra via $t\mapsto q_i^2$. In that algebra, if $yx=q_i^2xy$, then

$$ (x+y)^N=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-r)}\binom{N}{r}_i x^ry^{N-r},$$

using the symmetric Gaussian binomials of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. If instead $yx=t^{-1}xy$, the same expansion has coefficients $B_{N,r}(t^{-1})=t^{-r(N-r)}B_{N,r}(t)$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

derivations.claim: The adjoint action of $F_i$ on operators is $\operatorname{ad}(T)=F_iT-K_iTK_i^{-1}F_i$, and on $T=F_j$ one has $\operatorname{ad}^n(F_j)=\sum_{r=0}^{n}(-1)^rq^{r(m-n+1)}\binom{n}{r}_iF_i^{n-r}F_jF_i^r$ for every $n\ge0$, where $m=-a_{ij}$ is the $K_i$-weight of $F_j$ from [F1]. The case $n=0$ is the definition; the induction step multiplies the formula for $n$ on the left by $F_i$ and conjugates the rightmost factor, using $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q^mF_j$ and $K_iF_i^rK_i^{-1}=q^{-2r}F_i^r$ to move the toral elements, and the coefficient identity $\binom{n+1}{r}_i=q^{r}\binom{n}{r}_i+q^{r-n-1}\binom{n}{r-1}_i$ of [F4] (with $q$ replaced by $q_i=q$); the powers of $q$ combine to $q^{r(m-n)}$.

The finite Hom-space string bound. Fix $w\in W$ and let $U$ be its finite-dimensional rank-one submodule: for a homogeneous vector take the span of $F_i^aE_i^bw$, with finitely many $b$ by local nilpotence of $E_i$ and finitely many $a$ for each $b$ by local nilpotence of $F_i$; the rank-one commutator in [F2] makes this span stable. For a general vector sum the finitely many such spaces of its label components. Choose a finite basis of $U$ and let $U'$ be the sum of the finite rank-one submodules generated by its $F_j$-images. Then $F_j|_U$ belongs to the finite type-one rank-one module $\operatorname{Hom}(U,U')$, with operators $\mathcal K(T)=K_i'TK_i^{-1}$, $\mathcal E(T)=(E_i'T-TE_i)K_i$ and $\mathcal F(T)=F_i'T-\mathcal K(T)F_i$. Substitution of the rank-one relations verifies $\mathcal K\mathcal E\mathcal K^{-1}=q^2\mathcal E$, $\mathcal K\mathcal F\mathcal K^{-1}=q^{-2}\mathcal F$ and $[\mathcal E,\mathcal F]=(\mathcal K-\mathcal K^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$. Its integral weights lie in a finite set, so both weight-shifting operators are nilpotent. For $T=F_j|_U$, [F1] gives $\mathcal K(T)=q^mT$ and $\mathcal E(T)=0$. The highest-vector endpoint calculation in [F2] (or the rank-one proof of [F3], which uses no Serre relations) therefore gives $\mathcal F^{m+1}T=0$. Its expansion is exactly step 1.1 restricted to $U$, so $\operatorname{ad}^{m+1}(F_j)w=0$. No preservation of $U$ by $F_j$ is assumed.

The negative Serre sum vanishes. Put $n:=m+1=1-a_{ij}$. At $n=m+1$ the exponent in the expansion of step 1.1 is $r(m-n+1)=0$, so step 2.1 gives $0=\operatorname{ad}^{n}(F_j)=\sum_{r=0}^{n}(-1)^r\binom{n}{r}_iF_i^{n-r}F_jF_i^r$; as an operator identity on each $U$ containing $w$, hence on every vector $w\in W$ this is exactly the negative Serre sum.

The positive Serre sum vanishes. The Chevalley interchange of [F5] preserves all toral, toral-action and mixed relations used above and exchanges the roles of the $E$'s and $F$'s, so applying the argument of steps 1.1--3.1 to the image operators gives $\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r=0$ on every weight vector, hence as operators.

Conclusion. Under only the toral, toral-action, mixed-commutator and rank-one-integrability hypotheses, both quantum Serre sums of order $1-a_{ij}$ vanish, for every pair $i\ne j$ of the cyclic affine type $A$ datum, the cubic case included; no Serre relation was assumed.

For every $N\ge1$ the normally ordered wedges
$\{u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}:m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N\}$ of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]] form a
$\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $W_N$ and an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-basis of the
Laurent lattice $W_A$. The straightening algorithm terminates with a
well-founded profile: the total index sum and the ambient index interval are
preserved, secondary pairs become strictly more balanced in the sorted
dominance profile, and a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count;
in particular no bound by the initial inversion count alone is used. The
local $A_0$-chart $L_0:=A_0W_0$, where $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ and $W_0$
is the separate $\mathbb Z[q]$-span of the normal wedges, is a crystal basis: for each color $i$, on the occupied set of a normal tuple
the disjoint pairs $(u_{i+ke},u_{i+ke+1})$ behave as two-vertex highest-weight
$1$ strings, empty and doubly occupied pairs are frozen, and a shift of an
index by one either stays ordered or collides to zero; hence the residues of
the ordered wedges are stable under the normalized string operators and give a
crystal of the integrable affine wedge module. The image of the full
$\mathbb Z[q]$-tensor lattice need not equal $W_0$, and negative powers of $q$
in the straightening are not asserted to be triangular at $q=0$.

Let $F^{(M)}$ be the charge-$M$ Fock space with ground sequence
$b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ and let $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ be the opposite-channel energy.
Then:

(i) **Vanishing against the right tail.** For a fixed type-A ground sequence,
the condition $H_{\mathrm{op}}(b\otimes b^\circ_s)\le0$ means that the added
integer index lies inside or below the filled right tail
$\{M-s,M-s-1,\dots\}$; then $b\wedge b^\circ_s\wedge b^\circ_{s+1}\wedge\cdots=0$,
a sufficiently long finite prefix of this entire filled-tail wedge is already $0$, and hence the element lies in $q^nW_0$ for
every $n$.

(ii) **Dual left tail.** The mirrored condition with the left tail gives the
same exact finite vanishing, with the roles of left and right exchanged.

(iii) **Endomorphisms commuting with the loop.** A nonzero-weight endomorphism
$C$ of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ commuting with $z$ has only finitely many
loop-shift/color terms on each fundamental vector; inserting $C$ deep inside a
ground tail is eventually $0$, so it converges $q$-adically to $0$ on every
vector.

(iv) **The period operator.** For the explicit period operator
$T$ on $F^{(M)}$ that prepends $e$ vacuum entries and shifts every old index
down by $e$: $T$ preserves each label-weight/size component, and on the
positive-size-$n$ part its $k$-th power is $0$ as soon as $ke>n$.
Consequently $(1-T)^{-1}=1+T+T^2+\cdots$ is a finite geometric sum on every
nonvacuum weight, and each label weight has only finitely many partition
vectors.

Fix a **charge** $M\in\mathbb Z$ and let $W_N$ be the finite q-wedge spaces of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]. For $r\le s$ define
the connecting map
$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})
=u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}\wedge u_{M-r}\wedge u_{M-r-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-s+1}$,
so that new entries are the consecutive ground tail
$u_{M-N},u_{M-N-1},\dots$ appended to a prefix of length $N$. The **charge-$M$
Fock space** is the algebraic direct limit $F^{(M)}:=\varinjlim_{N}W_N$ of the
finite wedge spaces along these maps; equivalently it is the quotient of the
eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Write
$|\lambda;M\rangle$ for the image of the normally ordered semi-infinite word
with entries $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ indexed by the positive parts of the
partition $\lambda$, so that the vacuum $\varnothing$ corresponds to
$u_M\wedge u_{M-1}\wedge u_{M-2}\wedge\cdots$.

The **Laurent, positive and integral charts** of $F^{(M)}$ are

$$F_A:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_0:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A_0\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_{\mathbb Z0}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Z[q]\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}],\ A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}.$$

The **separated q-adic topology** on the full field space is the one induced by
the filtration $q^nF_0$, never by $q^nF_A=F_A$; a finite $A_0$-label component
completes to a $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$-lattice, and the full-field component completes
to $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$ for the label-weight
pieces. Separately, the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart completes to a
$\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$-lattice; this completion is not identified with
$\mathbb Q((q))$ and is not asserted to carry a $\mathbb Q$-vector-space
topology.

**Vacuum weights.** For $M=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$
the vacuum $P$-weight $\Omega_M$ is normalised by $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$ and
$\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$; explicitly, if $M=te+r$ with
$0\le r<e$, then

$$\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-\Bigl(\frac{e\,t(t-1)}{2}+tr\Bigr)\delta.$$

The weight of the partition $\lambda$ is
$\Omega_M-\sum_{\text{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, its size $|\lambda|$ is a separate
grading, and the $d$-eigenvalue is $\Omega_M(d)$ minus the number of residue-$0$
cells; no periodicity $\Omega_M=\Omega_{M-e}+\delta$ is asserted.

Let $\lambda\vdash n$ with Young diagram $[\lambda]$, and let
$\mu\vdash n-1$ and $\nu\vdash n+1$ denote partitions of the neighbouring
sizes ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

A node $x\in[\lambda]$ is **removable** if deleting it leaves a Young diagram,
that is, if there is a partition $\mu\vdash n-1$ with
$$[\mu]=[\lambda]\setminus\{x\};$$
such a $\mu$ is unique because a partition is determined by its diagram. A
point $y\notin[\lambda]$ is **addable** for $\lambda$ if inserting it leaves a
Young diagram, that is, if there is a partition $\nu\vdash n+1$ with
$$[\nu]=[\lambda]\cup\{y\};$$
again $\nu$ is unique. We write $\operatorname{Rem}(\lambda)$ and
$\operatorname{Add}(\lambda)$ for the sets of removable and of addable nodes
of $\lambda$.

Since $[\lambda]=\{(i,j):1\le i\le k,\ 1\le j\le\lambda_i\}$ is determined by
the inequalities $1\le j\le\lambda_i$, the two conditions have the following
row form. Write $\lambda_{k+1}:=0$ for a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$.
A node $(i,\lambda_i)$ is removable if and only if
$\lambda_i>\lambda_{i+1}$: deleting the last node of row $i$ keeps the row
lengths weakly decreasing exactly when row $i+1$ is strictly shorter, and no
node $(i,j)$ with $j<\lambda_i$ can be deleted, since the node
$(i,j+1)$ would then have no node to its left. Similarly a node
$(i,\lambda_i+1)$ with $1\le i\le k$ is addable if and only if $i=1$ or
$\lambda_{i-1}>\lambda_i$, the node $(k+1,1)$ opening a new row is always
addable, and these are all the addable nodes. In particular a row endpoint of
$[\lambda]$ is removable only if no node of $[\lambda]$ lies immediately
below it.

For the empty partition the diagram is empty, so
$\operatorname{Rem}(\varnothing)=\emptyset$, while
$\operatorname{Add}(\varnothing)=\{(1,1)\}$ is a single node, whose insertion
produces the partition $(1)$.

**Partitions.** Let $n\ge 0$ be an integer. A **partition of $n$** is a finite
weakly decreasing sequence $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$ of positive
integers with $\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_k=n$. Its entries are the **parts** of
$\lambda$ and $k$ is the **number of parts**. For $n=0$ the only partition is
the **empty partition** $\varnothing$, the empty sequence with $k=0$; for
$n\ge 1$ one has $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_k\ge 1$ and
$k\le n$. We write $\lambda\vdash n$. Trailing zeros are not parts: a finite
sequence of nonnegative integers ending in $0$ is not a partition, so the
number of parts of $\lambda$ is determined by $\lambda$ and
$(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$ is a different data type from
$(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k,0)$.

**English Young diagrams.** The **(English) Young diagram** of a nonempty $\lambda$ is
$$[\lambda]:=\{\,(i,j)\;:\;1\le i\le k,\ 1\le j\le \lambda_i\,\}\subseteq\mathbb N\times\mathbb N,$$
where $i$ numbers the **rows** downward and $j$ numbers the **columns**
rightward. An element of $[\lambda]$ is a **node**, or box, of the diagram. Row
$i$ of $[\lambda]$ carries $\lambda_i$ nodes, and column $j$ carries
$$\lambda'_j:=\#\{\,i: \lambda_i\ge j\,\}$$
nodes, a quantity that is $0$ beyond the last column (and for every $j\ge1$ when $\lambda=\varnothing$). Since a partition is weakly
decreasing, $[\lambda]$ determines $\lambda$: if $[\mu]=[\lambda]$, then row
$i$ of $[\lambda]$ is row $i$ of $[\mu]$, so $\mu_i=\lambda_i$ for every $i$
and $\mu=\lambda$. In particular $[\varnothing]=\emptyset$, the empty diagram.

**Conjugation.** The **conjugate partition** of a nonempty $\lambda$ is
$$\lambda':=(\lambda'_1,\lambda'_2,\dots,\lambda'_{\lambda_1}),$$
the sequence of column heights of $[\lambda]$, with $\varnothing':=\varnothing$
for the empty partition. This is again a partition of $n$, and
$[\lambda']$ is the transpose of $[\lambda]$:
for $1\le i\le\lambda_1$ and $1\le j\le k$,
$$(i,j)\in[\lambda']\iff j\le\lambda'_i\iff \lambda_j\ge i\iff (j,i)\in[\lambda].$$
Outside these bounds neither diagram contains the corresponding node; for the empty partition both diagrams are empty.
Conjugation is an involution, $\lambda''=\lambda$, because
$\lambda''_i=\#\{j:\lambda'_j\ge i\}$ counts the columns of $[\lambda]$ of
height at least $i$, that is, the columns $j$ with at least $i$ rows of length
$\ge j$, which by weak decrease is exactly the set of $j\le\lambda_i$. Thus
$\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ is a bijection on the partitions of $n$, exchanging
the number of parts with the largest part for nonempty partitions.

**Size zero.** The symmetric group of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ is
$S_n:=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\dots,n\})$ ([[def-symmetric-group]]) for every
$n\ge 0$, and we fix
$$S_0:=\operatorname{Sym}(\emptyset)=\{1\},$$
the trivial group; for $n=0$ the set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ is empty and the group
acts trivially on every size-zero object below. This is the convention used
whenever the constructions of this page are read at $n=0$.

Fix a **charge** $M\in\mathbb Z$ and let $W_N$ be the finite q-wedge spaces of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]. For $r\le s$ define
the connecting map
$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})
=u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}\wedge u_{M-r}\wedge u_{M-r-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-s+1}$,
so that new entries are the consecutive ground tail
$u_{M-N},u_{M-N-1},\dots$ appended to a prefix of length $N$. The **charge-$M$

with entries $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ indexed by the positive parts of the

$$F_A:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_0:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A_0\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_{\mathbb Z0}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Z[q]\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}],\ A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}.$$

topology.

$$\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-\Bigl(\frac{e\,t(t-1)}{2}+tr\Bigr)\delta.$$

On a prefix of length $N$ containing the support of $|\lambda\rangle$, the coproduct action of $F_i$ shifts a selected entry $i_k$ to $i_k+1$, provided $i_k\equiv i$; if $i_k+1=i_{k-1}$ the resulting term has a collision and vanishes by the wedge relations, and otherwise the shift is exactly the addition of the corner cell $(k,\lambda_k+1)$ of residue $i$ by [F3]. The $E_i$ formula. For $E_i$ the finite-prefix coproduct shifts an entry with $i_k\equiv i+1$ to $i_k-1$; if it collides the term is zero, and otherwise it deletes the corner cell $(k,\lambda_k)$ of residue $i$, whose smaller diagram is $\mu-\gamma$. The artificial removal at the cutoff duplicates the first appended ground entry and vanishes; after one more ground entry is appended, the same cancellation removes the changed boundary factor. Thus the renormalised operator is cutoff-independent and defines the stable limit by [F2]. The sign is negative because $E_i$ shifts down in the wedge.

The toral normalization. On a normal prefix of length $N$ extending past the partition's nonzero rows, the finite $K_i$ exponent is $N_i(\lambda)-\delta_{i\equiv M-N}$: the genuine corner pairs give the count, and the cutoff leaves one artificial occupied bottom of the pair $(M-N,M-N+1)$. Therefore the stabilized operator is $q^{\delta_{i\equiv M-N}}K_i^{[N]}$ after tail attachment and acts by $q^{N_i(\lambda)}$. For the degree torus, normalize the finite action by $q^{\Omega_{M-N}(d)}K_d^{[N]}$. The vacuum recurrence gives $\Omega_M=\Omega_{M-N}+\sum_{k=1}^N\mathrm{wt}(u_{M-k+1})$. Let $F^{(M)}$ be the charge-$M$ Fock space with ground sequence
$b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ and let $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ be the opposite-channel energy.
Then:

(i) **Vanishing against the right tail.** For a fixed type-A ground sequence,
the condition $H_{\mathrm{op}}(b\otimes b^\circ_s)\le0$ means that the added
integer index lies inside or below the filled right tail
$\{M-s,M-s-1,\dots\}$; then $b\wedge b^\circ_s\wedge b^\circ_{s+1}\wedge\cdots=0$,
a sufficiently long finite prefix of this entire filled-tail wedge is already $0$, and hence the element lies in $q^nW_0$ for
every $n$.

(ii) **Dual left tail.** The mirrored condition with the left tail gives the
same exact finite vanishing, with the roles of left and right exchanged.

(iii) **Endomorphisms commuting with the loop.** A nonzero-weight endomorphism
$C$ of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ commuting with $z$ has only finitely many
loop-shift/color terms on each fundamental vector; inserting $C$ deep inside a
ground tail is eventually $0$, so it converges $q$-adically to $0$ on every
vector.

(iv) **The period operator.** For the explicit period operator
$T$ on $F^{(M)}$ that prepends $e$ vacuum entries and shifts every old index
down by $e$: $T$ preserves each label-weight/size component, and on the
positive-size-$n$ part its $k$-th power is $0$ as soon as $ke>n$.
Consequently $(1-T)^{-1}=1+T+T^2+\cdots$ is a finite geometric sum on every
nonvacuum weight, and each label weight has only finitely many partition
vectors.

The constructed node operators on **all** partition vectors make the charge-$0$
partition Fock space $F$ into a $P$-graded integrable module for
$U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_e)$ with the fixed coproduct and the cyclic Cartan
datum: all toral commutation rules and mixed commutators
$[E_i,F_j]=\delta_{ij}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ hold, and both quantum Serre
sums vanish, including the cubic $e=2$ case with
$a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ and $[3]=q^2+1+q^{-2}$. Each color acts on finite Boolean
cubes, and $F_i,E_i$ change the $P$-weight by $\mp\alpha_i$. Ordinary standard
coefficients may have $q^{-1}$ poles; normalized Kashiwara lattice stability is
a separate statement.

Keep the conventions of the charge-$M$ Fock space
[[def-semi-infinite-q-wedge-fock-space-and-q-adic-topology]]. Normal wedges are
bijective with partitions through $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$; in charge $0$ the
vacuum is the empty partition. The stable finite-prefix action defines linear
endomorphisms $F_i,E_i,K_i,K_d$ of $F^{(0)}$ by

$$F_i|\lambda\rangle=\sum_{\text{addable }\gamma\text{ of residue }i}q^{A_i^r-R_i^r}\,|\lambda+\gamma\rangle,\qquad E_i|\mu\rangle=\sum_{\text{removable }\gamma\text{ of residue }i}q^{-(A_i^l-R_i^l)}\,|\mu-\gamma\rangle,$$

where for $F_i$ the counts are taken in the smaller diagram $\lambda$ and count
addable/removable $i$-nodes strictly to the right of the added node (higher
content), and for $E_i$ the counts are taken in the smaller diagram $\mu-\gamma$
and count nodes strictly to the left of the removed node (lower content), with
the removed node excluded; all sums are finite. The toral operators act by

addable-minus-removable count, and $K_d|\lambda\rangle=q^{-m_0(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$;
the size $|\lambda|$ is a separate grading. Charge $M$ replaces the residues by
content $+M$ and $K_d$ by $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$.

$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module over $\mathbb Q(q)$ for a finite symmetrizable
Cartan datum such that

(a) $M$ is a weight module with $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}M_\mu<\infty$ for every
$\mu\in P$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]);

(b) the weight set $\mathrm{wt}(M)$ is bounded above: it is contained in a
finite union $\bigcup_{j=1}^s(\lambda_j-Q_+)$;

(c) $M$ is integrable, i.e. $E_i$ and $F_i$ act locally nilpotently for every
$i$.

Then $M$ is isomorphic to an algebraic direct sum of simple integrable highest
weight modules $L(\lambda)$, $\lambda\in P^+$
([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]);
concretely, every nonzero submodule of $M$ contains a maximal vector $v$ whose
cyclic submodule $U_q(\mathfrak g)v$ is isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$ for some
$\lambda\in P^+$, and $M$ is the direct sum of the submodules generated by the
vectors of any maximal independent family of simple submodules. AC is used
exactly to select a maximal independent family of simple submodules
simultaneously; restricted to any module generated by one finite-dimensional
$U^{\ge0}$-submodule the decomposition is obtained by a finite induction and is
choice-free. The finite-cone modules use the explicit label grading, and the
regularization supplier is used when the original pairing is not separating
([[lem-finite-support-regularization-of-quantum-label-weight-modules]]).

with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules

$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, step 2.2).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
